questions.q: Concentrated aqueous sodium chloride is electrolysed with carbon electrodes. What forms at each electrode?
questions.why: Sodium is more reactive than hydrogen, so hydrogen forms at the cathode; chloride gives chlorine at the anode.

questions.q: Aqueous copper(II) sulfate is electrolysed using copper electrodes. What is observed?
options: anode loses mass; blue colour stays the same
anode gains mass; blue colour fades
bubbles at the anode; blue colour fades
bubbles at the cathode; anode gains mass
questions.why: The copper anode dissolves and copper is deposited on the cathode, so the Cu²⁺ concentration stays the same.

questions.q: During electrolysis, how is charge carried through the external circuit (the wires)?
options: by ions moving towards the cathode
by electrons moving through the electrolyte
by electrons moving from the anode to the cathode
by positive ions moving to the anode
questions.why: Electrons flow in the wires; ions carry the charge in the electrolyte.
